calls.title: Events Forwarder | Walk Through
calls.summary: The team discussed improvements to the event forwarder integration with Snowflake and BigQuery, focusing on UI redesigns to streamline setup processes. They agreed on the importance of access control, especially for enterprise users, and refined Snowflake connection settings, emphasizing the need for read-only critical fields to prevent errors. For BigQuery, the team examined schema management and emphasized the necessity of testing connections before saving changes. User experience enhancements were proposed, such as simplifying deletion prompts and archiving attributes while maintaining schema integrity. A commitment to automate fact table creation and queries was made, alongside a focus on Kafka connector management and ongoing research into cost-effective solutions.
calls.keywords: Event Forwarder, Snowflake, BigQuery, Fact Table, Experiment Assignment Queries, Data Source UI

calls.title: Events Forwarder | Walk Through
calls.summary: The meeting addressed the integration of the event forwarder within data source setup for Snowflake and BigQuery, prioritizing user clarity and ease of use. A new design was confirmed, replacing the old button with options for using either the event forwarder or a custom event tracker. Adjustments to sales messaging were discussed, ensuring enterprise users are directed to account managers. The team streamlined Snowflake access URL setup and clarified BigQuery settings for writes. Key decisions included automated fact table creation in BigQuery and locking event attributes post-setup to maintain data integrity. Cost considerations for connectors were highlighted, with a caution against multiple connectors due to their associated costs. Ongoing research on routing events was also noted for future enhancements.
calls.keywords: Event Forwarder, Snowflake, BigQuery, Fact Table, Experiment Assignment Queries, Data Source Configuration
